name: ZITLAS Oats Waffle with Peanut Butter
description: A crisp waffle made from an oats-egg batter, topped with peanut butter — a waffle format not used anywhere else in the database.
instructions: Blend ground oats, egg and milk into a smooth batter.
Cook on a hot, lightly greased tawa in a thick round, pressing lightly for a waffle-like crisp edge, 2-3 minutes per side.
Top with peanut butter and serve.
why_it_works: Waffle-style crisp texture is genuinely new to the database
No refined flour or added sugar
Quick, one-pan

name: ZITLAS Moong Dal Waffle
description: A savoury vegan waffle made from ground moong dal batter — distinct base and flavour from the sweet oats-egg waffle.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and ground — 70 g
instructions: Grind soaked moong dal into a thick batter with onion, cumin seeds and green chilli.
Cook on a hot tawa in a thick round, pressing for crisp edges, 3 minutes per side with a little oil.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Savoury, dal-based waffle format distinct from the sweet version
Fully vegan, high protein
Same technique gives users a choice between sweet and savoury

name: ZITLAS Chicken Tikka Wrap
description: Curd-marinated grilled chicken chunks rolled inside a roti — a non-vegetarian tikka format paralleling the Paneer Tikka Skewers but in wrap form.
instructions: Marinate chicken in curd and tikka masala for at least 15 minutes.
Grill or pan-sear until fully cooked, about 10-12 minutes.
Roll out and roast a roti.
Fill with the tikka chicken and roll tightly. Serve warm.
why_it_works: Wrap format is different from the skewer presentation of a similar marinade elsewhere
Lean chicken breast keeps fat moderate
Portable for a commute

name: ZITLAS Egg Muffin Breakfast Sandwich
description: A fried egg and toasted bread stacked into a fast-food-style breakfast sandwich — a distinct stacked construction from the toastie or bhurji sandwiches.
instructions: Fry the egg sunny-side up or over-easy in a little oil, seasoning with black pepper.
Toast two bread slices.
Stack the fried egg between the toasted bread.
Serve immediately while the yolk is warm.
why_it_works: Stacked, fried-egg sandwich is genuinely different from the whisked-omelette toastie already in the database
Extremely fast
Familiar fast-food-inspired format

name: ZITLAS Aloo Methi Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha with a mashed potato and fresh fenugreek leaf filling — a distinct vegetable-leaf pairing from any other paratha in the database.
instructions: Mix mashed potato with chopped fenugreek leaves, ajwain and chilli powder.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the mixture and seal.
Roll out and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Potato-and-methi combination is a distinct filling pairing from any single-ingredient paratha in the database
Classic North Indian winter combination
Filling, comfort-food breakfast

name: ZITLAS Rajma Galouti Kebab
description: Mashed, spiced rajma shaped into soft, pan-seared kebab patties — a kebab format and finer mash distinct from the chunkier Rajma Chaat or Poha Cutlet.
instructions: Blend boiled rajma into a very fine, smooth paste with ginger-garlic paste and garam masala (galouti kebabs are prized for their smoothness).
Mix in finely chopped onion.
Shape into small flat kebabs.
Pan-sear in oil until browned on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Fine-blended, melt-in-mouth kebab texture is distinctly different from the chunky cutlet or raw chaat uses of rajma elsewhere
Restaurant-style Lucknowi kebab technique made vegetarian
Fourth genuinely different rajma preparation in the database

name: ZITLAS Soya Seekh Kebab
description: Minced, spiced soya granules shaped onto skewers and pan-seared — a skewered kebab format distinct from the tikka-cube or loose-filling soya recipes elsewhere.
ingredients: Soya granules, rehydrated and ground — 80 g
instructions: Grind rehydrated soya granules coarsely and mix with onion, besan, garam masala and ginger-garlic paste into a firm dough.
Mould onto skewers (or shape into logs) into a seekh shape.
Pan-sear, turning frequently, until browned all over, about 8-10 minutes.
Serve with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Skewered log shape is a distinct format from the loose keema or wet sabzi soya preparations already in the database
Besan acts as a binder, a technique not used for soya elsewhere
Restaurant-style kebab made from an inexpensive protein

name: ZITLAS Chicken Seekh Kebab Roll
description: Minced chicken seekh kebab rolled inside a roti — a distinct non-vegetarian kebab-roll format from the tikka wrap.
instructions: Mix chicken mince with onion, garam masala and ginger-garlic paste, then shape into small logs.
Pan-sear, turning frequently, until fully cooked through, about 10-12 minutes.
Roll out and roast a roti.
Wrap the kebabs in the roti and serve warm.
why_it_works: Minced-and-shaped seekh technique is distinct from the cubed-and-marinated tikka technique already in the database
High protein, lean
Portable roll format

name: ZITLAS Egg Kejriwal Toast
description: A Mumbai-club-style fried egg on buttered toast topped with green chilli and coriander — an iconic distinct preparation from any other egg-on-toast recipe here.
instructions: Toast the bread lightly.
Whisk the egg with onion, green chilli and coriander, then cook it directly onto the toast in a pan (egg-topped-toast technique) until set.
Flip briefly to lightly toast the underside, then serve.
why_it_works: Iconic Mumbai club sandwich technique — egg cooked directly onto bread — is a distinct method from a separately-fried egg placed on toast
Genuinely different construction from the Egg Muffin Sandwich in this same batch
Bombay-style street food made simply

name: ZITLAS Moong Dal Pancake Stack
description: Small, thick savoury moong dal pancakes stacked like a Western pancake stack — distinct in format from the thin cheela or dosa preparations of moong dal elsewhere.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and ground — 70 g
instructions: Grind soaked moong dal with grated carrot and cumin seeds into a thick batter.
Cook small, thick rounds (about 6-7 cm) on a tawa, 2 minutes per side, until golden.
Stack 3-4 small pancakes.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Small, thick, stacked format is genuinely different from a single large thin cheela or dosa
Fun presentation for repeat use
Same reliable moong dal base, different construction

name: ZITLAS Paneer Do Pyaza Toast
description: Paneer cooked with a double portion of onion (do pyaza style) and spread on toast — a distinct onion-forward spice profile from any other paneer toast in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, saute a generous quantity of sliced onion until deeply softened and lightly caramelised, about 8 minutes.
Add paneer cubes, turmeric and coriander powder, cooking 2-3 minutes.
Toast the bread and spoon the paneer do pyaza over the top.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Do pyaza (double onion) technique gives a distinctly sweeter, more caramelised flavour than any other paneer preparation in the database
Restaurant-style flavour made simply
High protein toast option

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Idli Manchurian
description: Leftover or fresh idli cubed, pan-fried and tossed in an Indo-Chinese Manchurian sauce — a fusion format entirely distinct from any traditional idli preparation.
instructions: Toss idli cubes lightly in cornflour and pan-fry in a little oil until golden and slightly crisp on the outside.
In the same pan, saute garlic, capsicum and onion.
Add soy sauce and a splash of water, then toss in the fried idli cubes to coat.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Indo-Chinese fusion treatment of idli is a genuinely different eating experience from any traditional idli preparation in the database
Also works as a leftover-idli rescue recipe
Distinct sauce-based, stir-fried format

name: ZITLAS Paneer Manchurian Bowl
description: Pan-seared paneer cubes tossed in a light Indo-Chinese Manchurian gravy — a fusion sauce-based format distinct from the tikka, do pyaza or achari paneer preparations.
instructions: Lightly coat paneer cubes in cornflour and pan-sear until golden.
Saute garlic, capsicum and onion in the same pan.
Add soy sauce and a little water to form a light gravy, then toss in the paneer.
Simmer 2-3 minutes and serve hot.
why_it_works: Indo-Chinese gravy technique is a genuinely different flavour direction from any Indian-spiced paneer preparation elsewhere
Popular restaurant-style dish made at home with less oil
Sauce-based, distinct from dry preparations

name: ZITLAS Soya Chilli Bowl
description: Pan-fried soya chunks tossed dry in an Indo-Chinese chilli sauce — a dry fusion format distinct from the wet Manchurian gravy or Indian-spiced soya preparations.
ingredients: Soy sauce, garlic, green chilli — 6 g
instructions: Pan-fry rehydrated soya chunks until lightly browned.
Saute garlic, capsicum, onion and green chilli in the same pan.
Add soy sauce and toss everything together on high heat until mostly dry, about 3-4 minutes.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Dry chilli preparation is distinct from the wet Manchurian gravy earlier in this batch and from every Indian-spiced soya dish already in the database
High heat, quick tossing technique
Popular Indo-Chinese street food made vegetarian

name: ZITLAS Egg Fried Idli
description: Leftover idli pan-fried and tossed with scrambled egg — a leftover-rescue recipe using idli specifically, distinct from the Manchurian idli fusion.
instructions: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds, saute onion until soft.
Add cubed leftover idli and turmeric, tossing gently for 3-4 minutes until lightly crisp.
Push to one side, crack in the egg and scramble, then mix everything together.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Genuinely rescues leftover idli in a distinct, Indian-tempering-style preparation, different from the Indo-Chinese Manchurian treatment earlier in this batch
One-pan, quick
Higher protein than plain reheated idli

name: ZITLAS Chicken Stir-Fry Bowl
description: Lean chicken strips stir-fried with vegetables and served as a bowl without rice or bread — a low-carb, high-protein non-vegetarian bowl format.
instructions: Heat oil, saute garlic briefly.
Add sliced chicken and stir-fry on high heat until fully cooked, about 6-8 minutes.
Add capsicum and onion, stir-frying 2-3 more minutes until just tender.
Season with black pepper and serve as a bowl.
why_it_works: Low-carb, bread-free and rice-free bowl format, distinct from every other chicken preparation in the database
Very high protein-to-calorie ratio
Quick, single-pan preparation

name: ZITLAS Fish Tikka Skewers
description: Curd-marinated fish cubes grilled on skewers — a non-vegetarian tikka format using fish, distinct from the paneer or chicken tikka preparations.
instructions: Marinate fish cubes in curd and tikka masala for 20 minutes.
Thread onto skewers, alternating with capsicum.
Grill in an oven or air fryer at 200°C for 10-12 minutes, turning once, being careful not to overcook the fish.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Third fish recipe in the database, and the first grilled/skewered one, giving genuine format variety for fish
Very lean and high protein
Grilled, not fried

name: ZITLAS Curd Rajma Bowl
description: Boiled rajma folded into curd with light seasoning — a cold, creamy pairing distinct from every cooked or chaat-style rajma preparation in the database.
ingredients: Roasted cumin powder, black salt — 2 g
instructions: Fold boiled rajma into curd.
Season with roasted cumin powder and black salt.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.
why_it_works: Cold, creamy, no-cook format is distinct from every other rajma recipe (paratha, galouti, chaat, cutlet) elsewhere in the database
Two protein sources, entirely no-cook
Simple, cooling combination

name: ZITLAS Multigrain Vegetable Soup Bowl
description: A hearty vegetable soup thickened with a multigrain flour slurry — a vegan, grain-thickened soup distinct from the dal-based or egg-drop soups already in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, saute garlic and vegetables for 3-4 minutes.
Add water and bring to a simmer.
Whisk the multigrain flour with a little cold water into a slurry and stir in to thicken.
Simmer 6-8 minutes, season with black pepper, and serve hot.
why_it_works: Grain-thickened soup is a distinct technique from the egg-drop or dal-based soups already in the database
Fully vegan and vegetable-forward
Very low calorie, high volume

name: ZITLAS Paneer Bharta Toast
description: Roasted, then mashed and spiced paneer spread over toast — a bharta (roast-then-mash) technique distinct from the scrambled bhurji or grilled tikka preparations.
ingredients: Paneer, roasted whole then mashed — 80 g
instructions: Roast the whole block of paneer directly on a dry tawa until lightly charred on the outside, then mash it.
Heat oil, saute onion, add the mashed paneer, cumin powder and chilli powder, cooking 2-3 minutes.
Toast the bread and spread the paneer bharta over the top.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Roast-then-mash bharta technique gives a distinctly smoky flavour, different from the direct-crumble bhurji technique used for paneer elsewhere
Familiar bharta method (usually used for baingan or aloo) applied to paneer
Different mouthfeel from any other paneer spread

name: ZITLAS Baingan Paneer Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with roasted mashed eggplant (baingan) mixed with paneer — a vegetable-and-protein filling combination not used elsewhere in the database.
instructions: Roast the eggplant directly over a flame or in the oven until soft, then peel and mash.
Mix with crumbled paneer, cumin powder and chilli powder.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the mixture and seal.
Roll out and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Eggplant is a genuinely new vegetable for the database's parathas, with a distinct smoky flavour from roasting
Combines a vegetable bharta technique with a protein filling in one paratha
Different from any lauki, beetroot, methi or peas paratha already in the database

name: ZITLAS Karela Besan Chilla
description: A besan chilla batter with finely chopped, de-bittered bitter gourd (karela) mixed in — an unusual, nutritionally distinct vegetable rarely used in breakfast recipes.
ingredients: Karela (bitter gourd), finely chopped and salted — 50 g
instructions: Salt the chopped karela and let it sit for 15 minutes, then rinse and squeeze out the bitter liquid.
Whisk besan with water, cumin seeds and turmeric into a batter, then mix in the karela.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a round.
Cook until golden on both sides with a little oil.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Karela is a genuinely uncommon breakfast vegetable, included specifically for users seeking its distinct nutritional reputation in Indian home cooking
Salting technique manages the bitterness
Distinct flavour profile keeps the chilla rotation varied

name: ZITLAS Drumstick Leaves (Moringa) Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with chopped moringa (drumstick) leaves — a highly nutrient-dense leafy green not used anywhere else in the database.
instructions: Wash and finely chop the moringa leaves.
Mix with garlic and red chilli powder for the filling.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the leaves mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Moringa leaves have a notably higher protein and iron content than most leafy greens, genuinely distinct from spinach, methi or chaulai already used
A traditionally under-used but highly nutritious green in everyday Indian cooking
Distinct earthy flavour

name: ZITLAS Paneer Kali Mirch Wrap
description: Paneer cubes cooked in a black pepper (kali mirch)-forward sauce, wrapped in a roti — a distinct, sharply peppery spice profile from tikka, achari or do pyaza paneer.
instructions: Roll out and roast a roti; keep warm.
Heat oil, saute onion until soft, add paneer and a generous amount of crushed black pepper, cooking 3-4 minutes.
Stir in a spoon of curd to bring the sauce together.
Spoon the paneer onto the roti and roll tightly.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Black-pepper-forward spicing is a distinct flavour direction not used for paneer anywhere else in the database
Sharper, less sweet profile than do pyaza or achari versions
Restaurant-style dish adapted for a wrap

name: ZITLAS Egg Spinach Stuffed Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with scrambled egg mixed with cooked spinach — a distinct filling combination from either a plain egg-coated paratha or a palak-only filling.
instructions: Scramble the egg lightly, undercooking slightly since it will cook further inside the paratha, and mix with cooked spinach and black pepper.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the egg-spinach mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden and cooked through.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Combines egg and spinach directly inside a stuffed paratha, unlike the egg-coating technique or the spinach-only paratha elsewhere
Iron and protein combined in one filling
Distinct construction from any other egg paratha in the database

name: ZITLAS Chicken Salad Bowl
description: Cold, shredded boiled chicken tossed with vegetables in a no-cook salad — a distinct cold format from the stir-fry, bhurji or kebab chicken preparations elsewhere.
instructions: Boil and shred the chicken ahead of time.
Toss the cooled shredded chicken with cucumber and tomato.
Dress with lemon juice, a little oil and black pepper.
Chill briefly if possible and serve cold.
why_it_works: Cold salad format gives non-vegetarian users a no-cook option, unlike every other chicken recipe in the database which requires stovetop cooking at breakfast time
Very high protein, low calorie
Good for a weight-loss-focused morning

name: ZITLAS Fish Curry with Idiyappam
description: A light Kerala-style fish curry served with steamed idiyappam string hoppers — a distinct grain pairing from the fish-and-rice or fish-and-sandwich preparations elsewhere.
ingredients: Turmeric, mustard seeds, curry leaves — 4 g
instructions: Knead rice flour with boiling water and press into idiyappam strands; steam for 8-10 minutes.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, then add grated coconut and turmeric with a little water to form a light coconut gravy.
Gently add the fish and simmer 6-8 minutes until just cooked.
Serve the curry alongside the steamed idiyappam.
why_it_works: Idiyappam pairing is a genuinely different grain base from the rice pairing used for fish elsewhere in the database
Authentic Kerala combination
Light coconut gravy distinct from the mustard-oil Bengali fish curry

name: ZITLAS Paneer Jalfrezi Wrap
description: Paneer and julienned vegetables cooked jalfrezi-style in a tangy tomato-based sauce, wrapped in a roti — a distinct spice and vegetable-cut style from other paneer wraps.
instructions: Roll out and roast a roti; keep warm.
Heat oil, stir-fry julienned onion and capsicum on high heat for 2-3 minutes, keeping them crunchy.
Add tomato and jalfrezi spices, cooking until slightly saucy, then add the paneer strips and toss 2-3 minutes.
Spoon onto the roti and roll tightly.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Jalfrezi's signature julienned, still-crunchy vegetable cut is a distinct texture from the diced or cubed vegetables in every other paneer recipe here
Tangy tomato base is different from the creamy do pyaza or peppery kali mirch versions
Restaurant-style flavour in a wrap

name: ZITLAS Moong Dal Soup with Croutons
description: A moong dal soup topped with small toasted whole wheat bread croutons — distinct from the smooth Green Moong Soup Bowl by adding a crunchy textural element.
instructions: Pressure cook moong dal with tomato and water for 3 whistles until soft, then blend or mash smooth.
Heat oil, temper cumin seeds, and pour into the soup, seasoning with black pepper.
Toast bread cubes in a dry pan until crisp for croutons.
Serve the soup topped with croutons.
why_it_works: Croutons add a crunchy textural contrast not present in the earlier smooth moong soup, making this a genuinely different eating experience despite sharing a base
Bread adds extra carbs, making this a more complete meal than the plain soup
Simple, one-pot base

name: ZITLAS Chicken Clear Soup Bowl
description: A light, clear chicken broth with shredded chicken and vegetables — a distinct non-vegetarian soup format from the vegetarian soups already in the database.
ingredients: Chicken breast, boiled and shredded — 80 g
instructions: Boil chicken breast in water, reserving the broth, then shred the chicken.
Heat oil, saute garlic and vegetables briefly, then add the reserved broth.
Simmer 8-10 minutes, add the shredded chicken back in, and season with black pepper.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: First non-vegetarian soup in the database, genuinely different from the dal or vegetable soups elsewhere
Very high protein, very low fat
Light, good for a low-appetite or recovery morning

name: ZITLAS Egg Salad Sandwich
description: Mashed boiled egg mixed with curd and mustard, spread thick between bread slices — a mashed-salad spread distinct from the whisked-omelette toastie or fried-egg muffin sandwich.
instructions: Mash the boiled eggs with curd, mustard and black pepper into a thick, spreadable mixture.
Spread generously between two slices of bread.
Serve as is, or lightly toast if preferred.
why_it_works: Mashed egg-salad spread is a distinct texture from a fried egg or a whisked omelette used elsewhere in the database
Genuinely no-cook if the eggs are boiled ahead
Curd replaces the usual mayonnaise for a lighter version

name: ZITLAS Paneer Salad Wrap
description: Raw paneer cubes wrapped with fresh vegetables in a roti, entirely no-cook beyond the roti itself — distinct from every cooked paneer wrap or filling in the database.
instructions: Roll out and roast a plain roti; let it cool slightly.
Spread mint chutney on the roti.
Add raw paneer cubes and cucumber slices.
Roll tightly and serve — no cooking of the filling at all.
why_it_works: Using raw, uncooked paneer is a genuinely different approach from every cooked paneer preparation in the database, saving time and keeping the paneer's soft fresh texture
Very fast to assemble once the roti is made
Fresh, light eating experience

name: ZITLAS Chana Palak Bowl
description: A warm chickpea and spinach curry bowl — a distinct legume-and-green pairing from the chana chaat, sundal or ragda preparations elsewhere in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, temper cumin seeds, saute onion until soft.
Add spinach and cook until wilted.
Add boiled chana and garam masala with a splash of water, simmer 6-8 minutes.
Serve hot as a bowl.
why_it_works: Wet, spinach-forward curry format is distinct from the dry sundal, cold chaat, or wet-but-tomato-based ragda uses of chana elsewhere
High iron from spinach combined with chana's protein and fiber
Comforting, warming bowl

name: ZITLAS Rajma Tikka Skewers
description: Mashed, spiced rajma shaped onto skewers and grilled — a skewered kebab format distinct from the pan-seared galouti kebab earlier in this batch.
instructions: Mash boiled rajma with besan, onion and garam masala into a firm, mouldable mixture.
Shape onto skewers or into small logs.
Grill in an oven or air fryer at 200°C for 10-12 minutes, turning once.
Serve with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Grilled skewer format (dry heat) gives a different texture from the pan-seared galouti kebab earlier in this batch, despite using the same legume
Besan as a binder is a distinct technique from the finer blended galouti
Fifth genuinely different rajma preparation across the database

name: ZITLAS Sprouts Vegetable Soup Bowl
description: A light vegetable soup with mixed sprouts added for texture and protein — distinct from the smooth dal-based or clear chicken soups elsewhere.
instructions: Heat oil, saute garlic and vegetables for 2-3 minutes.
Add water and sprouts, bringing to a simmer.
Cook 8-10 minutes until the sprouts are just tender but still have some bite.
Season with black pepper and serve hot.
why_it_works: Sprouts keep some crunch, giving a genuinely different texture from the fully smooth or blended soups elsewhere in the database
High fiber and protein for a very light dish
One-pot preparation

name: ZITLAS Chicken Egg Kathi Roll
description: A roti dipped in egg (as in the Egg-Coated Paratha technique) and filled with spiced shredded chicken — combining two distinct techniques already in the database into one new roll.
ingredients: Chicken breast, boiled and shredded — 90 g
instructions: Roll out and dry-roast a roti until about 70% done.
Beat the egg and dip the roti in, coating one side, then return to the tawa egg-side down to set.
Separately, saute onion with shredded chicken and pav bhaji masala.
Fill the egg-coated roti with the spiced chicken, roll tightly, and serve warm.
why_it_works: Combines the egg-coating technique with a chicken filling, a genuinely new combination not tried elsewhere in the database
High protein from two sources at once
Popular Kolkata-style kathi roll construction

name: ZITLAS Tofu Clear Soup Bowl
description: A light, clear vegetable broth with tofu cubes — a vegan protein-soup option distinct from the chicken clear soup or dal-based soups elsewhere.
ingredients: Garlic, soy sauce, black pepper — 5 g
instructions: Heat oil, saute garlic and vegetables briefly.
Add water and bring to a simmer.
Add tofu cubes and soy sauce, simmering 6-8 minutes.
Season with black pepper and serve hot.
why_it_works: Vegan protein-soup option, distinct from both the chicken clear soup and the dal-thickened soups elsewhere in the database
Light Indo-Chinese flavour direction
Quick, one-pot

name: ZITLAS Paneer Tikka Wrap
description: The same curd-marinated grilled paneer used for the Paneer Tikka Skewers, but rolled inside a roti instead of skewered — a distinct eating format for the same marinade.
instructions: Marinate paneer cubes in curd and tikka masala for 15 minutes.
Grill or pan-sear until lightly charred, about 10-12 minutes.
Roll out and roast a roti.
Fill with the tikka paneer and roll tightly.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Wrap format gives users the choice between a plated skewer and a portable roll for the same marinade, mirroring the pairing already offered for chicken
Portable for a commute unlike the skewer version
Same reliable tikka technique

name: ZITLAS Roasted Chickpea Salad Bowl
description: Oven or air-fried roasted (crunchy) chickpeas tossed with vegetables — a crunchy-textured chana salad distinct from the boiled or sprouted versions elsewhere.
ingredients: Boiled chana, dried and roasted until crunchy — 100 g
instructions: Pat boiled chana completely dry, toss with a little oil, and air fry or oven-roast at 200°C for 15-20 minutes, shaking occasionally, until crunchy.
Cool slightly, then toss with cucumber, tomato and chaat masala.
Serve immediately while the chana is still crunchy.
why_it_works: Roasting to a crunchy texture is a genuinely different preparation from the soft boiled or crisp sprouted chana used elsewhere in the database
Air frying keeps this low in added fat
Distinct textural contrast within a familiar chana salad format

name: ZITLAS Moong Sprouts Salad Wrap
description: Raw moong sprouts and vegetables wrapped in a roti, entirely no-cook beyond the roti — a distinct no-cook wrap from the cooked cheela or dosa uses of moong sprouts.
instructions: Roll out and roast a plain roti; let it cool slightly.
Toss moong sprouts and cucumber with lemon juice and chaat masala.
Spoon onto the roti and roll tightly.
Serve immediately for maximum crunch.
why_it_works: Raw, crunchy sprouts wrapped cold are a genuinely different eating experience from the cooked uttapam or dosa uses of moong sprouts elsewhere
Minimal cooking beyond the roti itself
Fresh, light breakfast

name: ZITLAS Chicken Bharta Wrap
description: Boiled, shredded chicken mashed and spiced bharta-style, wrapped in a roti — a distinct mashed texture from the shredded stir-fry or minced seekh kebab chicken preparations.
ingredients: Chicken breast, boiled and finely shredded/mashed — 100 g
instructions: Boil chicken breast and mash/shred it very finely, closer to a paste than chunks.
Heat oil, saute onion, ginger-garlic paste and garam masala, then add the mashed chicken, cooking 4-5 minutes until well blended.
Roll out and roast a roti.
Spoon the chicken bharta onto the roti and roll tightly.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Very fine mash gives a distinctly smoother texture from the shredded stir-fry bowl or the coarser seekh kebab mince already in the database
Bharta technique applied to chicken, unusual outside vegetable bhartas
Third distinct chicken texture in the database

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Broth Poha
description: Poha cooked using a light vegetable broth instead of plain water — a flavour-layering technique distinct from every other poha preparation in the database.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 3 g
instructions: Simmer chopped vegetables in water for 8-10 minutes to make a light broth; strain, reserving both broth and vegetables.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, roast peanuts.
Add turmeric and the rinsed poha, then moisten with a few spoons of the vegetable broth instead of plain water, mixing gently.
Fold the cooked vegetables back in and serve hot.
why_it_works: Using a pre-made vegetable broth to moisten the poha, rather than plain water, is a genuinely different flavour-building technique from every other poha recipe in the database
Extracts more flavour from the vegetables than simply sauteing them
Still quick and familiar overall

name: ZITLAS Fish Pulao Bowl
description: A lightly spiced rice pulao cooked with flaked fish — a non-vegetarian rice-bowl format distinct from the fish curry or cutlet preparations elsewhere.
ingredients: Lean fish fillet, boiled and flaked — 100 g
instructions: Heat oil, temper whole spices, saute onion until golden.
Add rice and turmeric, then water in the standard ratio, and pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Gently fold in the flaked boiled fish once the rice is cooked, being careful not to break it up further.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Rice-pulao format is a distinct way to eat fish from the curry, tikka or cutlet preparations already in the database
One-pot, relatively low effort for a fish dish
Coastal home-style comfort food

name: ZITLAS Mixed Dal Soup Bowl
description: A soup made from a blend of three dals (moong, masoor, toor) simmered together — a broader-legume soup distinct from the single-dal moong soup already in the database.
instructions: Pressure cook the three dals together with tomato and water for 3-4 whistles until fully soft.
Blend or mash lightly for a smoother consistency.
Heat oil, temper cumin seeds and garlic, and pour into the soup.
Simmer 3-4 minutes and serve hot.
why_it_works: Combining three dals gives a broader amino acid and mineral profile than any single-dal soup already in the database
Genuinely different flavour from blending three pulses rather than using one
Simple, one-pot

name: ZITLAS Egg Salad Wrap
description: The same mashed curd-and-egg salad from the Egg Salad Sandwich, but rolled inside a roti instead of sandwiched in bread — a distinct format for the same filling.
instructions: Roll out and roast a plain roti; let it cool slightly.
Mash boiled eggs with curd, mustard and black pepper.
Spoon onto the roti and roll tightly.
Serve immediately.
why_it_works: Roti-wrap format is more portable than the bread sandwich version, giving users a choice for the same filling
Slightly different texture since the roti is softer than toasted bread
Good lunchbox alternative

name: ZITLAS Chicken Vegetable Pulao Bowl
description: A rice pulao cooked with chicken pieces and vegetables together — a non-vegetarian one-pot rice format distinct from the fish pulao or plain vegetable pulao.
instructions: Heat oil, temper whole spices, saute vegetables and ginger-garlic paste for 2-3 minutes.
Add chicken cubes and cook until sealed, about 4-5 minutes.
Add rice and water in the standard ratio, and pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Fluff gently and serve hot.
why_it_works: Chicken-and-vegetable-together pulao is a distinct one-pot format from the fish pulao (fish added after cooking) or the plain vegetable pulao elsewhere in the database
One-pot, minimal cleanup
Good family-portion breakfast if scaled up

name: ZITLAS Soya Do Pyaza Bowl
description: Soya chunks cooked with a double portion of onion, served over rice as a bowl — applying the do pyaza technique to soya instead of paneer, in a rice-bowl format.
instructions: Heat oil, saute a generous quantity of sliced onion until deeply softened, about 8 minutes.
Add soya chunks, turmeric and coriander powder, cooking 4-5 minutes.
Serve over warm rice in a bowl.
why_it_works: Applies the caramelised-onion do pyaza technique to a different protein (soya, not paneer) and a different serving format (rice bowl, not toast)
Fully vegan version of a restaurant-style technique
Different from every other soya preparation in the database

name: ZITLAS Paneer Chilli Bowl
description: Pan-fried paneer cubes tossed dry in an Indo-Chinese chilli sauce — a dry fusion format distinct from the wet Paneer Manchurian Bowl earlier in this batch.
ingredients: Soy sauce, garlic, green chilli — 6 g
instructions: Lightly coat paneer cubes in a little cornflour (or besan) and pan-fry until golden.
Saute garlic, capsicum, onion and green chilli in the same pan.
Add soy sauce and toss everything together on high heat until mostly dry, about 3-4 minutes.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Dry chilli technique is distinct from the wet Manchurian gravy for paneer earlier in this batch, mirroring the same dry-vs-wet distinction already established for soya
High-heat, quick tossing method
Popular Indo-Chinese dish made vegetarian and fitness-conscious

name: ZITLAS Rajma Soup Bowl
description: A blended, warm rajma soup — a sixth genuinely distinct rajma preparation in the database, this time in a smooth soup format.
ingredients: Cumin seeds, garlic, black pepper — 4 g
instructions: Blend boiled rajma with tomato and water into a smooth, thick soup.
Heat oil, temper cumin seeds and garlic, then pour in the blended soup.
Simmer 8-10 minutes, season with black pepper, and serve hot.
why_it_works: Smooth soup format is entirely different from the paratha, galouti, tikka, cutlet or curd-bowl uses of rajma elsewhere in the database
High fiber, warming, comforting
Quick, mostly hands-off

name: ZITLAS Chicken Manchurian Bowl
description: Pan-seared chicken cubes tossed in a light Indo-Chinese Manchurian gravy — the non-vegetarian counterpart to the Paneer Manchurian Bowl.
instructions: Lightly coat chicken cubes in cornflour and pan-sear until golden and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes.
Saute garlic, capsicum and onion in the same pan.
Add soy sauce and a little water to form a light gravy, then toss in the chicken.
Simmer 2-3 minutes and serve hot.
why_it_works: Completes the Manchurian pairing (paneer and chicken) already established for the fusion technique, giving non-vegetarian users the same option
High protein, moderate fat
Popular restaurant-style dish made leaner
